orders.judge: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Ramesh Ranganathan,Hon'ble Mr. Justice Alok Singh
orders.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL 
WRIT PETITION (PIL) NO. 149 OF 2015 
Paras Ram Joshi ………Petitioner. 
Versus 
State of Uttarakhand and others. …………Respondents. 
Mr. R.P. Nautiyal, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Mr. Tejas Agarrwal, learned counsel 
for the petitioner. 
Mr. S.S. Chauhan, learned Deputy Advocate General for the State of Uttarakhand. 
Dated: 10th December, 2018 
Hon'ble Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.
Hon'ble Lok Pal Singh, J.
 An extremely evasive and vague supplementary counter affidavit is 
filed, wherein no reference is made as to whether or not the petitioner’s 
village is now being supplied with drinking water. 
2. The reliefs sought for in this writ petition are for a mandamus 
directing the respondent authorities to install a water tank and pipelines 
as per the legal resolution dated 28.10.2009 of Mundhol Village 
Panchayat, Block Chakrata, District Dehradun; and for a mandamus, 
directing the State of Uttarakhand, to take necessary action against the 
concerned persons who misused the Government order dated 
31.03.2005, and misappropriated Government funds. 
3. Two schemes appear to have been prepared for supplying drinking 
water to Mundhol Village Panchayat and, while serious irregularities are 
said to have taken place in implementation of the second scheme, the 
Principal Secretary has stated, in his letter, that there could not have been 
any financial irregularities since implementation of the scheme has 
resulted in Government money being saved in the process. In the 
supplementary counter affidavit, all that is stated is that the scheme has 
been successfully implemented. However, enclosed with the very same 
supplementary counter affidavit, is a letter dated 19th December, 2012 
sent by the Executive Engineer to the Chief Engineer, Minor Irrigation 
Department, Uttarakhand Dehradun, along with the report dated 
18.09.2012, which discloses that the drinking pipeline, supplying water 
to the subject village, has been damaged. If successful implementation 
of the scheme is mere laying of a pipeline without water being actually  2
supplied to the villagers, then the action of the authorities must be 
faulted. What is even more disconcerting is that the Joint Secretary, who 
filed this supplementary counter affidavit, has not even chosen to state 
whether or not drinking water is being supplied to the villagers 
concerned. 
4. We consider it appropriate, in such circumstances, to direct the 
Joint Secretary to be personally present in Court on the next date of 
hearing along with the entire records to enable us to ascertain, whether or 
not drinking water is now being supplied to the petitioners’ village. 
5. Sri S.S. Chauhan, learned Deputy Advocate General, is present in 
Court and undertakes to inform the Joint Secretary of his obligation 
under this order. 
6. Post on 17.12.2018 in the daily cause list. 
 
(Lok Pal Singh, J.) (Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.)
 10.12.2018 10.12.2018 
Rathour

orders.judge: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Ramesh Ranganathan,Hon'ble Mr. Justice Ramesh Chandra Khulbe
orders.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
WRIT PETITION (PIL) No. 149 of 2015
Paras Ram Joshi ………..Petitioner. 
Vs. 
State of Uttarakhand and others. ...Respondents 
Mr. R.P. Nautiyal, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Mr. Tejas Agarrwal, learned counsel for the 
petitioner. 
Mr. S.S. Chauhan, learned Deputy Advocate General for the State of Uttarakhand. 
Dated: 17th December, 2018
Coram: Hon’ble Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.
 Hon’ble R.C. Khulbe, J.
Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J. (Oral) 
 The report of the Lok Ayukt dated 04.07.2012 makes 
disconcerting reading. The Lok Ayukt has pointed out that as against 
an extent of 415 meter recorded in the “M” Book, only 379 meter 
length of pipeline was found to have been laid on physical 
verification; there was a variation of 36 meter length of pipeline; in 
another area, while the length of the pipeline is reflected in the “M” 
Book as 935 meters, on physical verification, only 835 meter length of 
pipeline was found on the ground; and, thereby, there was a short fall 
of 82 meter length of pipeline. The Lok Ayukt had identified certain 
officers who were responsible, and had recommended that an FIR be 
lodged against them, and the matter be investigated by police officials. 
2. Curiously, a high powered committee was constituted, 
(consisting of one Executive Engineer and two Assistant Engineers 
from the very same Department whose officers are alleged to have 
misappropriated funds), which absolved all these officers, and opined 
that these pipelines were damaged because of land-slide. The report 
does not, however, disclose as to when the land-slide took place, as 
also the basis for their conclusion that the damage to the pipelines was 
on account of a land-slide. The place, where land-slide had allegedly 
occurred, is also not reflected in the said report.  2
3. Prima facie, it does appear that the Committee, of 
officers of the very same Department, was constituted only to cover 
up the entire issue and to absolve those, who were guilty of 
misappropriation of funds earmarked for utilization in the Schemes to 
provide irrigation and drinking water needs of the subject villagers, of 
all blame. While the report of the Lok Ayukt and the Committee’s 
report are both of the year 2012, and more than 6 years have since 
elapsed, no action appears to have been taken to repair the damaged 
pipelines even till date, and the villagers are, for no fault of their, 
being deprived of much needed water both for drinking and irrigation 
purposes. 
4. While Sri S.S. Chauhan, learned Deputy Advocate 
General, on instructions, would submit that, in certain areas, the open 
canals were damaged by the villagers themselves to ensure that water 
flows into their lands, what is not stated is the efforts, if any, made by 
the Department to identify the culprits who had damaged the pipeline 
/ canal, and why no action was taken against them. 
5. If the pipeline had been damaged because of a land-slide, 
then the villagers concerned cannot be said to have damaged the 
pipeline for its flow into their fields. If, on the other hand, the 
pipeline was damaged by the villagers, the question of it being 
damaged by land-slide would not arise. Further, even if the pipeline 
had been damaged because of land-slide, there would be remnants of 
the pipeline traceable in the area. It is also not clear whether the area, 
where these pipelines were found missing, are areas which suffered 
from a land-slide or not. These issues can be resolved, and the 
persons responsible for such lapses identified, upon a counter affidavit 
being filed by the Chief Engineer who, we are told, heads the 
Department of Irrigation. 
6. The Chief Engineer will submit a detailed counter￾affidavit explaining the basis on which the three member Committee 
had arrived at the conclusion that the officers, named in the report of  3
the Lok Ayukt were above blame; and the time frame within which 
damaged pipelines will be repaired to ensure that water (both for 
irrigation and drinking purposes) is made available to the villagers. 
6. Post on 2nd January, 2019. 
7. Let a certified copy of this order be issued, by 
19.12.2018, on payment of the prescribed charges. 
 (R.C. Khulbe, J.) (Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.)
17.12.2018 17.12.2018 
Rathour

orders.text:
WPPIL No. 149 of 2015 
Hon’ble Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.
Hon’ble R.C. Khulbe, J.
Mr. R.P. Nautiyal, learned Senior Counsel 
assisted by Mr. Prashant Khanna, learned counsel 
for the petitioner. 
Mr. C.S. Rawat, learned Additional Chief 
Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand￾respondent nos. 1 to 3. 
While it is asserted in the affidavit filed by the 
Chief Engineer and HOD, Minor Irrigation 
Department, Dehradun that the pipeline, through 
which water was being supplied, was earlier 
damaged because of natural calamities; and a part of 
the pipeline was broken by the family members of 
the petitioner himself to let water into their fields, it 
is also stated that water is now being supplied to the 
subject Village. 
This submission is vehemently denied by Mr. 
R.P. Nautiyal, learned Senior Counsel appearing on 
behalf of the petitioner. 
The only way in which this assertion of the 
Chief Engineer can be verified is if the District 
Judge, Dehradun is requested to depute a Judicial 
Officer to visit the site and ascertain whether water, 
for irrigation and drinking purposes, is being made
available to the residents of the subject village. 
A copy of this order shall be forthwith 
transmitted to the District Judge, Dehradun who is 
requested to submit his report by 05.02.2019. 
The petitioner and the Chief Engineer shall be 
put on notice by the officer deputed to the site, and 
the inspection shall be caused in their presence or in 
the presence of their representatives. 
Post this case on 11.02.2019 
 (R.C. Khulbe, J.) (Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.)
 07.01.2019 07.01.2019
